greek: Καὶ εἶπεν κύριος ὁ θεὸς πρὸς Νωε Εἴσελθε σὺ καὶ πᾶς ὁ οἶκός σου εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν, ὅτι σὲ εἶδον δίκαιον ἐναντίον μου ἐν τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ.
hint: Noah is told to go in with all his house, the word Hebrews 11:7 uses of the ark's purpose.

notes.text: οἶκος is first *a house, abode, dwelling*, then *household goods, substance*, then *household, family*. Hebrews 11:7 says Noah built the κιβωτός εἰς σωτηρίαν τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ.
δίκαιος, *observant of custom and social rule*, as at 6:9.
[[flag]] The Hebrew has *YHWH* alone; the Greek adds ὁ θεός.
Glossed again, first in this chapter.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν κτηνῶν τῶν καθαρῶν εἰσάγαγε πρὸς σὲ ἑπτὰ ἑπτά, ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ, ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν κτηνῶν τῶν μὴ καθαρῶν δύο δύο, ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ,
hint: The clean animals appear for the first time, seven by seven.

notes.text: καθαρός is first *clear of dirt, clean, spotless*, then *clear, open*, and in a moral sense *clear from pollution, pure*. The Hebrew is *haṭṭĕhôrâ*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *šibʿâ šibʿâ ʾîš wĕʾištô*, *seven seven, a man and his wife*, and of the unclean *šnayim ʾîš wĕʾištô*. The Greek has *male and female*, the words of 1:27.
εἰσάγω, *to lead in*, the verb of 6:19, now an aorist imperative.

hint: The Greek adds unclean birds, which the Hebrew does not mention.

notes.lemma: καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν πετεινῶν τῶν μὴ καθαρῶν δύο δύο
notes.text: [[flag]] Not in the Hebrew, which has only *of the birds of the heavens, seven seven, male and female*. The Greek adds *clean* to those birds and a second clause for the unclean, matching 7:2.
The Hebrew is *lĕḥayyôt zeraʿ*, *to keep seed alive*. διατρέφω has one sense in Middle Liddell, *to sustain continually*, so it is plain text.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʿal-pĕnê kol-hāʾāreṣ*, *upon the face of all the earth*. The Greek has no *face*.

greek: ἔτι γὰρ ἡμερῶν ἑπτὰ ἐγὼ ἐπάγω ὑετὸν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τεσσαράκοντα ἡμέρας καὶ τεσσαράκοντα νύκτας καὶ ἐξαλείψω πᾶσαν τὴν ἐξανάστασιν, ἣν ἐποίησα, ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς γῆς.
hint: The Hebrew's 'every living substance' is a Greek word Paul uses for resurrection.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *kol-hayqûm*, *all that stands, every living substance*, from *qûm*, *to rise, stand*. The Greek renders the root: ἐξανάστασις, *a rising up from*, which Middle Liddell glosses *resurrection* and knows only from Philippians 3:11, εἰς τὴν ἐξανάστασιν τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν. At 7:23 the same Hebrew word is ἀνάστημα. Codex Alexandrinus reads πᾶν τὸ ἀνάστημα here too, as Rahlfs's apparatus records.
ἐξαλείφω's first sense is *to plaster* or *wash over*, used of walls; *to wipe out, obliterate* is its second. The Hebrew *ʾemḥeh* is *I will wipe out*, as at 6:7, where the Greek had ἀπαλείφω.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾānōkî mamṭîr*, *I am causing it to rain*. The Greek has *I bring rain*, with ἐπάγω, the verb of the deluge at 6:17.
νύξ is, in Middle Liddell's words, *night*, either *the night-season* or *a night*; the first tagged translation is *the night-season*.

greek: καὶ ἐποίησεν Νωε πάντα, ὅσα ἐνετείλατο αὐτῷ κύριος ὁ θεός.
hint: Noah does all that he was commanded, as at 6:22.

notes.lemma: καὶ ἐποίησεν Νωε πάντα, ὅσα ἐνετείλατο αὐτῷ κύριος ὁ θεός
notes.text: The words of 6:22, without its closing οὕτως ἐποίησεν.
[[flag]] The Hebrew has *YHWH* alone; the Greek adds ὁ θεός.

notes.text: *The deluge of water came to be*. The Hebrew *wĕhammabbûl hāyâ mayim* sets *the flood* and *waters* side by side. [[flag]] Rahlfs prints ἐγένετο ὕδατος from Papyrus 911 alone; Codex Alexandrinus alone has ἦν.
Genitive of age, as at 5:32; the Hebrew is *a son of six hundred years*.

hint: Luke 17:27 and Matthew 24:38 quote the entry into the ark word for word.

notes.text: Matthew 24:38 and Luke 17:27 both have ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας εἰσῆλθεν Νῶε εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *mippĕnê mê hammabbûl*, *from before the waters of the flood*: plural waters, and *face* in the preposition. The Greek has διά, *because of*, and the singular, as at 1:2.

[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾărubbōt haššāmayim*, *the windows of the heavens*, in the plural. καταρράκτης as a noun is *broken water, a waterfall*, then *a portcullis*, then *a gull*, the bird that rushes down.
Both passive: ῥήγνυμι, *to break*, and ἀνοίγνυμι, *to open*, in that voice. The entry's own passive glosses, *to burst* and *to stand open*, follow in the chains.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyisgōr YHWH baʿădô*, *and YHWH shut behind him*. The Greek adds τὴν κιβωτόν and ὁ θεός, and has ἔξωθεν, *from without*. Codex Alexandrinus puts τὴν κιβωτόν before ἔξωθεν αὐτοῦ.
A neuter plural subject with a singular verb.

reading: and [[the ones going into|the ones going into, the ones entering]] [[male|male, the male sex, masculine and strong, mighty]] and [[female|female, the female sex and womankind, belonging to women, feminine, fresh and refreshing, tender and delicate and gentle, soft and yielding and weak]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] [[of flesh|of flesh, of the flesh, of muscles, of the body, of man's nature generally]] [[went in|went in, went into and entered, came into, came in, came upon]], [[according as|according as, just as, like as if, exactly as]] [[enjoined|enjoined, commanded]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] to [[name:Νωε]]. and [[shut|shut, closed, barred, shut up and blocked, confined]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[from without|from without, outside, without and free from]] him [[the wooden box|the wooden box, the chest, the coffer]].

greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὁ κατακλυσμὸς τεσσαράκοντα ἡμέρας καὶ τεσσαράκοντα νύκτας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἐπληθύνθη τὸ ὕδωρ καὶ ἐπῆρεν τὴν κιβωτόν, καὶ ὑψώθη ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς.
hint: The Greek adds forty nights to the Hebrew's forty days.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has *ʾarbāʿîm yôm*, *forty days*, and no nights here.
ἐπαίρω is first *to lift up and set on*, then *to lift, raise*; ὑψόω, *to lift high, raise up*. John 3:14 and Acts 2:33 use ὑψόω of the Son of Man lifted up and exalted, the entry's second sense.

reading: And [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] [[the deluge|the deluge, the inundation]] forty [[days|days, day-breaks, times]] and forty [[night-seasons|night-seasons, nights, watches of the night, darknesses of night, nights of death]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]], and [[was made full|was made full, was increased, was multiplied, was in the majority, prevailed]] the water and [[lifted up and set on|lifted up and set on, lifted and raised, exalted and magnified, stirred up and excited, induced and persuaded]] [[the wooden box|the wooden box, the chest, the coffer]], and [[was lifted high|was lifted high, was raised up, was elevated and exalted]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]].

greek: καὶ ἐπεκράτει τὸ ὕδωρ καὶ ἐπληθύνετο σφόδρα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἐπεφέρετο ἡ κιβωτὸς ἐπάνω τοῦ ὕδατος.
hint: The Hebrew's 'face of the waters' returns, and the Greek drops it again, in the words of 1:2.

notes.lemma: ἐπεφέρετο ἡ κιβωτὸς ἐπάνω τοῦ ὕδατος
notes.text: The words of 1:2, where πνεῦμα θεοῦ ἐπεφέρετο ἐπάνω τοῦ ὕδατος: the same verb, the same preposition, the same singular water. [[flag]] The Hebrew here is *wattēlek hattēbâ ʿal-pĕnê hammāyim*, *the ark went upon the face of the waters*. The Greek drops *face*, as it did at 1:2, and *face of the waters* must not appear.
Three imperfects, where the Hebrew has narrative past tenses. ἐπικρατέω is *to rule over*, then *to prevail*; the Hebrew *wayyigbĕrû* is *prevailed*.

reading: and [[was ruling over|was ruling over, was holding power, was prevailing and conquering, was getting the mastery, was superior]] the water and [[was being made full|was being made full, was being increased, was being multiplied, was being in the majority, was prevailing]] [[very|very, very much, exceedingly, violently, far, most certainly]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]], and [[was being brought upon|was being borne along, carried over, swept upon, brought continuously to bear]] [[the wooden box|the wooden box, the chest, the coffer]] over and atop the water.

greek: τὸ δὲ ὕδωρ ἐπεκράτει σφόδρα σφοδρῶς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐπεκάλυψεν πάντα τὰ ὄρη τὰ ὑψηλά, ἃ ἦν ὑποκάτω τοῦ οὐρανοῦ·
hint: The Greek doubles the adverb, as the Hebrew doubles 'very'.

notes.text: The Hebrew is *mĕʾōd mĕʾōd*, *very very*. σφόδρα is *very, exceedingly, violently*; σφοδρῶς is the adverb of σφοδρός, *vehement, violent*.

notes.lemma: ἐπεκάλυψεν πάντα τὰ ὄρη … ὑποκάτω τοῦ οὐρανοῦ
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is passive, *all the high mountains were covered*, and has *under all the heavens*. The Greek makes the water the subject, and has *under the heaven*.
A neuter plural with a singular verb, as at 7:16.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], the water [[was ruling over|was ruling over, was holding power, was prevailing and conquering, was getting the mastery, was superior]] [[very|very, very much, exceedingly, violently, far, most certainly]] [[vehemently|vehemently, violently, excessively, impetuously, strongly and robustly]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]] and [[covered over|covered over, covered up, shrouded, put as a covering over]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[the mountains|the mountains, the hills]] [[the high|the high, the lofty, the high-raised, the highland, the stately]], which was [[below|below, under]] [[of the heaven|of the heaven, of the vault, of the firmament and the sky]];

greek: δέκα πέντε πήχεις ἐπάνω ὑψώθη τὸ ὕδωρ καὶ ἐπεκάλυψεν πάντα τὰ ὄρη τὰ ὑψηλά.
hint: Fifteen cubits above, the water was lifted high.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ḥămēš ʿeśrê ʾammâ milmaʿlâ gābĕrû hammayim*, *fifteen cubits upward the waters prevailed*, and *the mountains were covered*. The Greek has *was lifted high* and, again, *covered all the high mountains*.
Printed as two words, as at 5:10: *fifteen*.
Without a genitive, an adverb; plain text as at 1:2.

reading: fifteen [[fore-arms|fore-arms, arms, centrepieces of the bow, horns and sides of the lyre, cubits and ells, cubit-rules]] upon, over, and atop [[was lifted high|was lifted high, was raised up, was elevated and exalted]] the water and [[covered over|covered over, covered up, shrouded, put as a covering over]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[the mountains|the mountains, the hills]] [[the high|the high, the lofty, the high-raised, the highland, the stately]].

greek: καὶ ἀπέθανεν πᾶσα σὰρξ κινουμένη ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς τῶν πετεινῶν καὶ τῶν κτηνῶν καὶ τῶν θηρίων καὶ πᾶν ἑρπετὸν κινούμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος.
hint: All flesh that moved on the earth died.

notes.text: The Hebrew is *wayyigwaʿ*, *expired*, the verb the Greek rendered τελευτήσει at 6:17.
The Hebrew has two verbs, *hārōmēś*, *creeping*, and *haššereṣ haššōrēṣ*, *the swarm that swarms*. The Greek has κινέω for both.

greek: καὶ πάντα, ὅσα ἔχει πνοὴν ζωῆς, καὶ πᾶς, ὃς ἦν ἐπὶ τῆς ξηρᾶς, ἀπέθανεν.
hint: The Hebrew's 'breath of the spirit of life in its nostrils' is shorter in Greek.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *kōl ʾăšer nišmat-rûaḥ ḥayyîm bĕʾappāyw*, *all in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life*. The Greek has πνοὴν ζωῆς, the words of 2:7, with no *spirit* and no *nostrils*.
ξηρός is *dry*; as a noun, ἡ ξηρά, *dry land*, its one noun sense, so it is plain text. The Hebrew is *beḥārābâ*.

reading: and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]], [[as great as|as great as, as much as, as far as, as long as, as many as]] [[has|has, holds, possesses, keeps, dwells in and inhabits, holds fast, bears up against and supports]] [[a blowing|a blowing, a blast, a breeze, a breathing hard, breath, flame]] [[of a living|of a living, of the means of life and substance, of life and existence, of a way of life]], and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]], who was [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] of the dry land, [[died off|died off, died, was put to death, was slain]].

greek: καὶ ἐξήλειψεν πᾶν τὸ ἀνάστημα, ὃ ἦν ἐπὶ προσώπου πάσης τῆς γῆς, ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπου ἕως κτήνους καὶ ἑρπετῶν καὶ τῶν πετεινῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἐξηλείφθησαν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς· καὶ κατελείφθη μόνος Νωε καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ κιβωτῷ.
hint: The Hebrew word of 7:4 returns, and the Greek gives it a second word.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *kol-hayqûm* again, which the Greek rendered ἐξανάστασις at 7:4. ἀνάστημα is not in Middle Liddell; LSJ's first sense is *height*, then *protuberance*, *high ground*, *building*.
ἐξαλείφω, *to plaster*, as at 7:4, in the passive.
The Hebrew is *wayyiššāʾer ʾak-nōaḥ*, *only Noah was left*.

greek: καὶ ὑψώθη τὸ ὕδωρ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἡμέρας ἑκατὸν πεντήκοντα.
hint: A hundred and fifty days, as in the Hebrew.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyigbĕrû*, *prevailed*, as at 7:18–20; the Greek has *was lifted high*.
150, as in the Hebrew.
